intro: This cloud icon draws a simple puffy cloud outline, the shorthand for online storage and services running on remote servers. Use it to mark files that are synced or backed up, link to a drive, show sync status or label hosting and cloud settings in developer and admin tools.
meaning: Network diagrams drew the internet as a cloud long before cloud computing had a name, so the shape came to mean somewhere off your device. People read it as storage, sync and backup. With an up arrow it means upload, with a down arrow download, and with a slash it means offline or not synced. Keep it apart from weather icons by leaving out sun and rain.
uses: File manager list: marks files stored online only, separate from those downloaded to the device.
Photo app settings: labels the backup section showing how many photos are safely copied online.
Hosting control panel: opens the servers area where admins start, stop and resize virtual machines.
Note-taking app header: shows sync status, turning into a crossed cloud when changes are waiting to upload.
tips: Use small badges on the cloud for state, such as a tick for synced or an arrow for uploading, rather than separate icons.
In weather or travel apps, avoid this plain cloud for storage features, because people will read it as an overcast forecast.
Pair sync status changes with text like Saved or Offline, since many users never notice a small cloud changing shape.

faq.q: What does a cloud storage icon usually look like?
faq.a: It is usually a plain cloud outline, sometimes with a tick, an arrow or a small drive inside. It tells people the files live online rather than only on the device, so it suits drive links, backup settings and sync status.

faq.q: Which icon works for cloud upload?
faq.a: For a cloud upload icon, add an upward arrow inside the cloud or place an upload arrow beside it. The arrow carries the action and the cloud says where the file is going. Use the plain cloud for status and the arrow version for buttons.
